subject: Private deployment: preflight scheduling and rollback template
messages:
From: Jill Price <jill.price@acmehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Health Infra <infra@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Private infra upgrade request — canary + rollback constraints

Aditya,

We're planning to move our private deployment (VPC) to Redwood runtime 1.4.2 to pick up the security backports and new KV cache behavior. As a healthcare customer this needs to land inside our approved maintenance windows (SLA window: Thu 02:00–06:00 UTC or Sun 22:00–02:00 UTC) and we need a clear rollback template and evidence of a dry-run prior to production.

Key constraints:
- No >15m sustained downtime per service surface (we can tolerate brief token-generation slowdowns)
- Need canary on 2 pods (single-customer hosts) for 6 hours before wide rollout
- Audit artifacts for a compliance review (pre/post telemetry & audit logs)

Can you propose a schedule and a rollback plan we can present to the change board? Attached is our current network diagram (acme_network_diagram.pdf) — note the customer VPC peering and HA DB replicas.

Thanks,
Jill Price
Head of Infrastructure
ACME Health

Attachments: acme_network_diagram.pdf
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jill Price <jill.price@acmehealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 13:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private infra upgrade request — canary + rollback constraints

Jill — thanks for the diagram and the constraints. We can accommodate both windows; proposed plan below and a couple of clarifying Qs.

Proposed maintenance windows (pick one):
- Primary: Sun, 2028-08-28 22:00–02:00 UTC (preferred — aligns w/ ACME's low-traffic window)
- Alternate: Thu, 2028-08-31 02:00–06:00 UTC

Canary & rollout approach (high level):
1) Preflight dry run in your staging VPC 72h prior to primary window (we'll coordinate a 2hr run)
2) Canary: update 2 dedicated customer nodes (hostnames: acme-node-canary-{1,2}) and monitor for 6h
3) Gradual ramp: 10% -> 40% -> 100% over 3 maintenance batches (30–45m windows) with KV cache joins paused between batches
4) Post-checks: latency P99, error spike check, audit log shipment verification (S3)

Rollback (quick summary):
- Immediate: toggle version-pin at routing layer to prior image (we keep 1.3.9 pinned)
- Evacuate new pods, re-route traffic to pinned nodes; KV caches will fall back to on-disk mode — expected transient latency increase
- If we cannot restore within 20m of the rollback start, escalate to a full failover to the standby region (requires your approval)

Clarifying items:
- Do you require DB schema migrations? (should be none for this runtime bump)
- Confirm whether audit artifacts must be uploaded to your S3 bucket or a Redwood-provided retention store

I'll follow up with an internal runbook and an attached checklist. Looping in Dev, Laura and Markus to own canary, rollback automation and ops runbook.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Attachments: patch-checklist.xlsx (internal runbook stub)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 13:20:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: ACME private upgrade — preflight & rollback runbook (draft)

Team — draft runbook below. This will be provided to ACME after we validate the dry-run in staging. Please confirm owners/actions.

Runbook (concise):
- PREP (T-7d):
  * Verify ACME dev/staging mirror exists and is network-equivalent (Laura)
  * Create snapshot of customer-specific KVS and confirm export (Dev)
  * Confirm S3 bucket write permission and audit-log target (Markus)
  * Create blue/green canary nodes and pin 1.3.9 on standby nodes (Aditya)
- DRY RUN (T-3d):
  * Execute upgrade in staging -> run smoke suite (15m), hold 1h observation
  * Validate telemetry ingestion and audit log integrity (Markus)
  * Mock rollback and measure expected restoration time (Dev)
- MAINTENANCE (Go/No-Go checklist):
  * Pre-window: ensure support on-call and DB read replicas in sync
  * During window: drain non-critical requests, disable scheduled batch jobs, set KV cache TTL to 0 for nodes being upgraded
  * Canary: upgrade acme-node-canary-1 then -2; 6h observation between canary and ramp
  * Ramp: 10% -> 40% -> 100% with health gating at each step; automatic abort on >3% error or 25% P99 latency increase
- ROLLBACK (steps):
  * Step 1 (immediate): Re-pin routing to 1.3.9, spin up pinned nodes from kept AMIs/images
  * Step 2 (5–15m): Drain new nodes; failover incoming requests to pinned nodes
  * Step 3 (15–30m): Rehydrate caches from snapshot (note: may cause spike in background IO)
  * Step 4 (>30m): If service still degraded, trigger standby-region failover (requires ACME ops signoff)
- POST-MORTEM:
  * Capture console logs, topology diff, and audit shipment; provide artifact bundle for compliance review

Automation notes:
- We'll add a single CLI toggle (rw rollout pin set --customer acme --version 1.3.9) that reverses routing at the edge — Dev to own the toggle implementation.
- Add a preflight Jira (RW-1523) that runs smoke and logs pass/fail to the change record.

Owners: Dev=toggle/rollback automation, Laura=staging validation & scheduling, Markus=telemetry & audit

Please review and ack changes. I'll fold this into a customer-facing PDF and send to Jill once we have confirmation on the requested window.

— Aditya

We also want the explicit rollback SLA: full restoration to 1.3.9 within 30 minutes of rollback start or we escalate to standby region failover (we own the final signoff).

Can you confirm you will:
- Do a dry-run on staging 2028-08-25 (preferred time window 18:00–20:00 UTC)
